summary: No relevant testing skill found. Email/password registration, persistence, duplicate signup, correct login, wrong-password login, unknown-email login, homepage H1, and UI toast flows passed. Google OAuth redirect button passed, but Google sign-in is still not fully fixed: AuthCallback exchanges the same OAuth session_id twice under React StrictMode, which can turn a one-time OAuth session into an error.

integration_issues.issue: AuthCallback.jsx lacks a StrictMode-safe processed guard; a simulated OAuth return to /#session_id=fake_session_id produced 2 POST /api/auth/session calls and then displayed the Google login failure toast. Because Emergent OAuth session_id values are one-time use, this can break real Google sign-in. This diagnostic used a MOCKED /api/auth/session response because real Google credentials/session_id were unavailable.

action_items: Make AuthCallback StrictMode-safe by using a useRef processed guard set synchronously before the async /auth/session exchange, and/or clear/replace the URL hash before exchanging so the same session_id cannot be submitted twice.
Retest Google OAuth callback end-to-end after the guard is added.
critical_code_review_comments: AuthCallback.jsx currently uses useEffect without a processed guard while the app is rendered inside React.StrictMode in index.js. The Emergent auth playbook warns this exact pattern can cause duplicate one-time session exchange requests.
Landing.jsx Google redirect construction is correct: window.location.origin + '/home' encoded in https://auth.emergentagent.com/?redirect=.
seed_data_creation: Created random test users via API/UI, including bugtest_1785346998_7344@lovreski.ru and additional bugui_<timestamp>@lovreski.ru accounts; they remain in MongoDB as evidence of persistence.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend auth endpoints passed exact status/detail checks and MongoDB persistence. UI auth toasts and hero H1 passed. Recheck only the Google OAuth callback after fixing duplicate /api/auth/session calls; the current diagnostic MOCKED /api/auth/session and observed two calls under React.StrictMode.
rca_of_the_issue: React.StrictMode mounts/effects twice in development. AuthCallback.jsx posts the OAuth session_id inside useEffect without a useRef hasProcessed guard. A Playwright diagnostic returning to /#session_id=fake_session_id with a MOCKED one-time /api/auth/session route showed two exchange calls and the second failure caused the user-visible Google auth error toast.
